content:
Yes, this is from an infamous early instant message conversation that Mark Zuckerberg had as a Harvard student, shortly after launching "The Facebook" in 2004. He was talking about how users were willingly giving him their personal information.

The conversation became public years later and has been widely cited as evidence of Zuckerberg's early cavalier attitude toward user privacy. In the exchange, he reportedly called the users who trusted him "dumb fucks" (though you didn't include that part in your quote).

This quote has followed Zuckerberg throughout his career and is often brought up in discussions about Facebook/Meta's approach to user data and privacy.
